name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Greg Stanton holds a roughly 4-to-1 cash advantage over Zuhdi Jasser with no outside spending against him
Prediction markets price Stanton around 95 percent to win
District leans Democratic and the national environment component favors Democrats this cycle
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, leaving the margin less precisely measured
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: Stanton is a well-funded incumbent in a D+4 district, Jasser has raised only modestly, and markets price Stanton near 95 percent. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based estimate with a slight discount for the third-party candidate and thin data.
model.watch: Any late-breaking polling, outside spending against Stanton, or a sharp shift in the national environment could narrow what is currently a wide expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Greg Stanton, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this Phoenix-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, roughly $2 million on hand compared with about $340,000 for Republican Zuhdi Jasser, and no outside groups are spending against him. Jasser, a repeat challenger, has run a low-budget campaign, and a No Labels candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Stanton's chances around 95 percent. With the incumbent's money advantage, name recognition, and a favorable district, Stanton is the clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
